triage.note: BURNED HELD-OUT CASE, moved here 2026-08-28, and the burn is of the rarer kind: the FIX made a FROZEN LABEL WRONG, so changing the label is influence and the case cannot stay held out. The label was `min_chars: 16 >= 100`, authored 2026-08-17 and NEVER RUN, from an independent tag-strip scan that counted headings and anchor occurrences — it never measured a span. Simon Property Group FY2019's item 16 body is, in full, the word `None.`; no floor above about 35 characters is satisfiable, so the label asserted something the filing does not contain. It passed until 2026-08-28 for the wrong reason: item 16 was the last item, so its span ran to the signature block and swallowed the 23 KB EXHIBIT INDEX the filing typesets after it — the ADR-042 §g defect, confirmed independently on Simon FY2024 (23,401 chars) and MetLife FY2024 (38,153). The floor was being cleared by the bug. With `ANNEX_RE` clipping the last item at a trailing annex, item 16 is 65 chars and correct, and the case went red. ADJUDICATED: the pipeline is right and the frozen label is wrong. The three checks that replace it say what is actually true and would catch the bug's return — the body is `None.`, the span is under 200 chars, and the exhibit index is not inside it. Recorded rather than quietly relabelled: a held-out label overturned by its own subject is exactly the event this README's burn rule exists to make visible.
